data.title: The Crypto-Key Sync
data.statement:
You are an infiltration specialist hacking into a high-security mainframe. The mainframe has deployed a firewall that demands a numeric synchronization token.

The firewall hands you a massive string of data chips containing numbers ([[nums]]), and a single [[target]] frequency. To bypass the security block, you must find <<exactly two different data chips>> whose values add up to the [[target]] frequency.

Once found, you must output the <<indices>> (0-based positions) of those two chips. The firewall only processes data sequentially, so you must find the answer before the system's strict timeout window lapses!

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

You are an infiltration specialist hacking into a high-security mainframe. The mainframe has deployed a firewall that demands a numeric synchronization token.

The firewall hands you a massive string of data chips containing numbers (nums), and a single target frequency. To bypass the security block, you must find exactly two different data chips whose values add up to the target frequency.

Once found, you must output the indices (0-based positions) of those two chips. The firewall only processes data sequentially, so you must find the answer before the system's strict timeout window lapses!
Input
Line 1: An integer target (the sum you need to reach).

Line 2: An integer N (the total number of elements in the array).

Line 3: N space-separated integers representing the array nums
Output
Two space-separated integers representing the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target. (Output the smaller index first).
Constraints
2 ≤ N ≤ 1000
-10^9 ≤ target ≤ 10^9
-10^9 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10^9
Example
Input
9
4
2 7 11 15
Output
0 1
